what.text: This page follows refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina living in Norway, as counted by UNHCR at the end of each year.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 896 refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina in Norway, 3.6% of all refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Serbia and Kosovo is the largest host of refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by France and Denmark.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflicts in Bosnia-Herzegovina from 1992 to 1995, over Serb, Croat and Bihaca Krajina territory.
The main years of displacement in the data, 1997 to 2002, come after those conflicts ended.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 1997 at 13783 refugees.
The figure was at its highest, 14385, at the end of 2001, and has fallen since then.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in Norway.
These are year-end totals for Norway only, reported to UNHCR.
